Subject: Re: VPC pricing structure + RFP follow-up

Daniel —

Appreciate the RFP, and good questions. Summary answers below and an ask for one confirmation so we tailor the commercials exactly to your usage profile. High-level:

1) Pricing split model (recommended)
   • Operator / Site license: one-time charge covering operator seats, cluster activation keys, and perpetual deployment entitlement per-site.
   • Platform fee: recurring monthly fee that covers the control plane, telemetry, patches, and access to model catalog + minor feature updates.
   • Amortization: we commonly support procurement amortization over 24 months for the platform fee on the commercial contract (two options: invoice monthly with capital approval note, or invoice annually with an amortization schedule in the SOW).

2) SRE retainer vs. service credits
   • Option A (SRE retainer): fixed monthly hours + guaranteed SLA response ladder. Best for teams that want predictable support capacity during rollout.
   • Option B (migration service credits): commit to a platform fee band and receive a bank of credits to redeem against migration hours or risk-mitigation incidents within the first 6 months.
   • We can mix: reduce retainer by up to 30% if you take a migration credit bank equal to X hours.

3) Support tiers (Standard vs Enterprise) — on-prem VPC callouts
   • Standard: business-hours support, 48-hour P1 response target for on-prem-specific incidents, monthly patches, email-only escalation.
   • Enterprise: 24x7 coverage, 4-hour P1 response, named SRE on-call during migration window, proactive runbooks and quarterly operational reviews.

Attachment: Draft_SOW.csv (CSV with sample amortization table and migration-credit calculations)

One confirmation we need from you: estimated average tokens/day and % of peak burst above that baseline during first 90 days — this drives the platform fee band and any burst allowance. If you can send a quick ballpark we’ll produce a counterproposal by tomorrow.

Best,

Subject: INTERNAL: AvaTech deal — commercial approach and concessions (notes)

Eve / Soojin / Marissa —

Quick internal notes for the proposal to Daniel — please comment inline. Goal: protect unit economics while offering procurement-friendly mechanics.

Key pieces to present (recommended):
- Base structure: One-time operator license + monthly platform fee. Target platform-band = $35k–$55k/month depending on tokens/day.
- Amortization: we allow 24-month amortization for the platform fee. If they choose annual invoicing we can offer a 2% discount.
- Migration credits: offer 200 hours of migration credits (redeemable in first 6 months) in lieu of a full SRE retainer; credits value = $72k.
- SRE retainer (optional): $18k/month for 40 hours/month during onboarding (4-week heavy phase) then tapered to 10 hours/month.
- Concession corridor: up to 12% discount on platform fee in exchange for a 24-month committed volume and a 10% non-refundable pilot tranche payment.
- Exit protection: 90-day migration assistance at 50% hourly rate if they do a migration within 12 months of contract termination.

Risks / asks:
- Need accurate token estimate (see Eve's note) — without that we risk under-sizing the platform band.
- Avoid open-ended unlimited burst; cap burst allowance to 2x baseline for the first 90 days then evaluate.

Suggested messaging to procurement: be explicit about amortization mechanics (we can put the amortization schedule into SOW so procurement can capitalize the spend).

If no objections I’ll draft a concise grid for Eve to send to Daniel (numbers + two alternative commercial bundles).

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: internal_pricing_notes.txt (internal)

Daniel —

Thanks — based on the RFP and a short internal calibration we propose two commercial bundles tailored to procurement and capital planning needs. I’ve put the details in the attached Draft_SOW.csv and included a short summary below. If either bundle looks good we will prepare a redline-friendly SOW + DocuSign link.

Bundle A (Pilot-friendly) — 12 month term- Operator license: one-time $120,000 (per primary site)- Platform fee: $38,000/month (includes telemetry, control plane, minor updates)- Migration credits: 200 hours (redeemable in first 6 months)- Support: Standard tier during steady-state; Enterprise during migration window for first 8 weeks- Amortization: we will include a 24-month amortization schedule in the SOW for capital teams- Concession: 6% discount on platform fee with a 10% non-refundable pilot tranche

Bundle B (Commit + discount) — 24 month term- Operator license: one-time $110,000- Platform fee: $33,000/month (committed band)- Migration credits: 150 hours + optional SRE retainer at $12k/month for first 3 months- Support: Enterprise tier for first 12 weeks- Concession: 10% discount on platform fee with 24-month committed volume

Common notes:
- Burst policy: baseline + 2x burst allowance for first 90 days; any sustained overage billed at agreed per-token tiers.
- Exit/migration assistance: offered at 50% of hourly rate for first 90 days post-contract if required.
- We will provide an amortization appendix so procurement can capitalize the platform fee if desired.

Next steps:
1) If you can confirm a ballpark tokens/day (or attach a recent usage sample) we’ll finalize the banding.
2) If you prefer Bundle B we’ll draft a 24-month SOW with the amortization appendix and a draft DocuSign.

Attachments: Draft_SOW.csv (sample amortization tables + credits math), Redwood_Terms_2026.docx

Looking forward — can hop on a 30m call early next week if you want to walk through the SOW.
